subject: infra.connect
name: 2026 Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity for Africa
milestone: Adopted at the CPL-26 ministerial meeting, 2026-07-24
position_end: Adopted, committing member states to technology-neutral regulation, continental harmonisation, fair access to spectrum and fibre, shared infrastructure and data governance; the text itself is not published
note: The full text was sought by the acquisition pass on 2026-07-30 and not obtained

subject: infra.connect
name: Africa Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Report
milestone: Request for proposal for Phase 1 issued 2026-08-03, closing 2026-08-18
position_end: Phase 1, Country Pilots, put out as an open consultancy tender at a stated budget of US$165,000, funded jointly by the African Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance; the pilot countries and the terms of reference are not established
note: The terms of reference sit behind the AIIB procurement portal and were not retrievable at ingest; an acquisition line was filed 2026-08-09

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile internet users and their measured economic value
milestone: Industry association figures cited 2026-08-12
position_end: 416 million Africans used mobile internet in 2025, generating a measured US$240bn of economic value, put at 7.8% of continental GDP
note: an industry association’s own modelled value, cited in a secondary account

subject: infra.store
name: Data centres the AfCFTA Secretariat states digital trade requires
position_end: More than 700, against about 220 on the continent, on the Secretary General's statement at Marrakech
sources: 2026-04-08 Africa's digital trade push requires 700 data centres, says AfCFTA chief
note: The Secretariat's own estimate, not an independent count

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign AI cloud on edge data centres
milestone: Partnership announced 2026-08-17
position_end: Announced: AI processing units hosted inside an African edge data-centre network, sold as locally-hosted enterprise AI
note: a vendor partnership between [AI] Analytics Intelligence and Open Access Data Centres, a WIOCC Group company, announced on the vendors' own channel; the stated offering is AI processing units inside OADC's edge sites with industry-specific applications for financial institutions, pitched at data-sovereignty and regulatory-compliance demand. No site list, capacity, price, launch date or customer is published, so the sovereignty claim rests on hosting location alone and nothing here establishes where the models, weights or operator control sit

subject: infra.store
name: Time for a data centre to reach 85% occupancy
position_end: Six to eight years in African markets against two to three in Europe, on the Africa Data Centres Association's 2026 Economic Report, which also puts 80-90% of the continent's data as still processed and stored abroad and projects the market at US$9.2bn by 2029
note: An industry association's own report; the occupancy and offshore-processing figures carry no stated method.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reported cybercrime losses across the continent
milestone: Continental cyberthreat assessment reported 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13
position_end: About US$484m reported, more than double the 2024 figure, drawn from 36 member countries, with artificial intelligence involved in 55% of surveyed 2025 cybercrime cases and deepfake incidents up sevenfold between the second and fourth quarters of 2024; against that, only 8% of intelligence analysts are recorded as having advanced artificial-intelligence expertise and 94% of agencies as lacking digital forensics tools, and a single Ugandan deepfake investment scam is put at over US$2m of losses
note: the figures are an international police organisation’s own assessment, reaching the base through two secondary accounts

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Vendor-measured attack volume across the continent
milestone: July 2026 reading published 2026-08-13
position_end: African organisations averaged 3,237 attacks a week in July 2026 against a global average of 2,336, behind Latin America at 3,561 and Asia-Pacific at 3,316; Angola was highest of the African markets broken out at 5,714, then Nigeria at 4,975, Kenya at 2,915 and South Africa at 2,195. Ransomware victims were up 87% year on year and the continent posted the world's highest phishing rate at 1 in 106 emails
note: a single vendor's telemetry from its own installed base, not a national or continental measurement; the sample, denominator and country coverage are not published, and it is a different series from the reported-loss figures collected from member countries

subject: dpi.exchange
name: ADAPT (Africa Digital Access and Public Infrastructure for Trade)
milestone: Stated in pilot in Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco, second Digital Trade Forum, Lagos, 2026-07-02
position_end: In pilot in Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco on the Secretary-General's statement to the second Digital Trade Forum; no live exchange, governing instrument or assessment held
note: Held through Data Landscapers analysis, which is cited as named third-party analysis; the pilot is stated by the Secretary-General and no implementation document is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AfCFTA Customs Modernisation Project
milestone: US$3.1bn contract signed with a private supplier
position_end: A public-private partnership under which Bergmans Security Consultants and Supplies Limited mobilises the financing for customs digital solutions, secure electronic exchange of customs information, coordinated border management, One Stop Border Posts, transit systems, electronic cargo tracking, non-intrusive inspection technology, integrated data centres, multilingual customs portals, risk management and data analytics across participating State Parties; the agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding concluded in July 2026 and nothing is recorded as deployed; a US$3.1bn contract was signed with a Nigerian security consultancy to digitise customs across the 50 member states, aiming at real-time cargo tracking and reduced revenue leakage
note: The concession agreement is not published; how Bergmans is repaid over twenty years, which State Parties have acceded and on what instrument, and who controls the data in the integrated data centres are stated by neither party. The Secretary-General's figure of about 50 countries signed on is uncorroborated and no list is published; the contract value and the supplier come from a press account rather than a published award notice, and the same account frames payment friction as the larger trade barrier

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Data Policy Framework
milestone: Endorsed by the AU Executive Council, February 2022
position_start: In force since February 2022 as the continental reference for data governance, with none of its operative texts drafted
position_end: Unchanged in text; the three operative frameworks it provides for went to validation in December 2025 and none is adopted or published
note: The English file on au.int is a 2024 reissue of the February 2022 instrument, not a later edition

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Digital Agriculture Strategy implementation
milestone: Continental harmonisation workshop held 11 to 13 August 2026
position_start: Adopted for 2024-2030 with an average agricultural growth target of 6 per cent and an estimated US$165 million continental implementation cost, prioritising national e-agriculture strategies over a uniform regional approach after a 2021 situation analysis covering all 55 member states
position_end: A continental workshop convened regional economic communities, union organs and participating countries to harmonise implementation, seeking interoperable agricultural data platforms, common data governance and alignment of national and regional systems with the continental digital transformation strategy and agriculture reporting
note: no member-state implementation count or timetable is published; the US$165 million is the strategy’s own continental estimate rather than a committed funding line

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Guidelines for Integrating Data Provisions in Protocols on Digital Trade
milestone: Issued September 2023
position_start: Issued September 2023 as a reference guide for negotiators integrating data provisions into the AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade
position_end: Unchanged; no record is held of its provisions being carried into the Protocol or its annexes
note: The cover date is September 2023; the AU posted the document on 2025-05-22

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Continental data governance frameworks
milestone: Validation workshop, Addis Ababa, 1-4 December 2025
position_end: Three drafts - data categorisation and data sharing, cross-border data flows, and a continental open data strategy - validated with member states and regional economic communities; none submitted to AU policy organs and none published
note: Run under the Data Governance in Africa Initiative, funded by BMZ and the European Union and implemented with AUDA-NEPAD and GIZ

subject: dpi.exchange
name: IGAD SDMX regional statistical-systems capacity-building programme
milestone: Four-day capacity-building and technical-assistance programme on SDMX convened by the Secretariat, supported by the African Development Bank
position_end: Outcome stated as harmonised SDMX Data Structure Definitions and a long-term roadmap institutionalising SDMX across IGAD and its member states under Open Data Portal 2.0; no budget, adoption date or roadmap milestone published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Member-state implementation status of the AU Data Policy Framework

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SADX (Smart Africa Data Exchange)
milestone: Cross-border digital identity pilot running between Rwanda, Ghana and Benin
position_end: Unveiled at Conakry on 2025-11-12 and taken into a technical mission with Rwanda, Benin and Ghana on trust chains, interface contracts and incident response; no live exchange held; the alliance and a German development agency say a digital identity issued in one of Rwanda, Ghana or Benin is now recognised in the other two, with eighteen further countries said to be joining, presented as the first step to a single African digital market by 2030

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Smart Africa cross-border data exchange guidelines
milestone: Drafted by eleven member states at Rabat, 2025-07
position_start: Drafted by eleven member states under the Council of African IT Agencies
position_end: No adopted text, signatory list or implementation record held in the year since the drafting session
sources: 2025-07-14 Smart Africa co-creates Africa's first Cross-Border Data Exchange Guidelines (Rabat, ADD-chaired CAITA)

subject: dpi.id
name: ADLI cohort on the AfCFTA Digital Identity Annex
milestone: Cohort convened with the AfCFTA Secretariat
position_end: Six countries across three trade corridors working on compliance with the annex, on a test-and-learn basis; no assessment or mutual-recognition decision held
sources: 2026-05-27 Africa's economic future hinges on breaking down silos. This ADLI cohort advances integration

subject: dpi.id
name: APAI-CRVS (Africa Programme on Accelerated Improvement of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)
milestone: The 2017-2026 APAI-CRVS decade closing and a 2027-2036 phase opening, reported 2026-08-10
position_end: The 2017-2026 decade is closing and a 2027-2036 phase is opening; the African eCRVS Shared Asset (ACSA) is named as the shared continental standard intended to cut fragmented digital procurement across country systems, and Equatorial Guinea's Justice Ministry timed a free registration campaign for children aged 0-5 (10-14 August 2026) to the decade's close. No AU statement of the new phase's content, financing or targets is held
note: Both sources are secondary to the AU: a practitioner argument piece and a member-state campaign notice. The APAI-CRVS phase documents themselves are not held, so the new phase is recorded as opening rather than as adopted

subject: dpi.id
name: Continental ID and data-protection law analyser
milestone: Launched 2026-08-11
position_end: An open-source tool launched by a university research network comparing identity and data-protection laws across more than 50 African countries, built as a retrieval-augmented chatbot and stated as intended to help states harmonise their frameworks; no usage figure, governance arrangement or maintenance commitment is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Association of African Central Banks (AACB)
milestone: 47th Assembly of Governors, Yaounde, 2025-11-28
position_start: No decision of the Assembly on continental payment harmonisation held
position_end: A list of 54 decisions, of which decision 21 rules that the Payment Systems Directive for Africa is not to be led by an entity external to central banks and directs its own task force to lead the work

subject: dpi.pay
name: Banks and countries connected to PAPSS
position_start: 28 banks within nine months of launch, against an ambition of all 500 to 600 African banks (2022)
position_end: 28 countries and over 190 banks and financial-technology firms connected, with the Central African central bank acceding in July 2026 and the West African central bank's pilot pending; connecting the EAC, West, Central and Southern African regional systems is put at reaching more than 60% of African countries, and no continent-wide transaction value is published (2026-08)
sources: 2026-08-17-africa-single-payments-market-currencies-divided|2026-08-10-telegraph-papss-africa-financial-system-beyond-dollar|2026-02-04 PAPSS, Onafriq launch new trade rail for West Africa|2026-03-02 Pesalink and PAPSS link networks for African payments|2022-08-30 Pan-African Payment and Settlement System drives Africa's banking integration
note: a separate account puts the system at 19 of the 55 member states as at 2025, so the reach figures held are not reconciled with each other; AfricaNenda's deputy chief executive puts the binding constraint on the currency side rather than the rail - more than 40 currencies, many not directly convertible, forcing settlement banks, correspondent banking and pre-funded accounts, with regulatory harmonisation on licensing and settlement named as the condition for cutting costs

subject: dpi.pay
name: CARICOM Payment and Settlement System (CAPSS)
milestone: Barbados and the Bahamas central banks complete proof of concept; Ghana proposes Caribbean access to AfCFTA with local-currency settlement, Kingston, 2026-08-02
position_start: Did not exist; modelled on PAPSS since CARICOM governors' unanimous October 2023 selection
position_end: Proof of concept complete in two countries; the ECCB Governor says at least two more central banks are needed for the initial pilot; not commercially operational, with settlement, FX, liquidity, AML and interoperability arrangements unresolved

subject: dpi.pay
name: COMESA digital retail payments platform
milestone: Scheme rulebook and a gender strategy to 2030 published 2026-08-10
position_end: The regional clearing house published the scheme rulebook setting operational and governance rules for instant low-cost cross-border retail payments, and a gender audit and strategy to 2030 drawn from research along the Malawi-Zambia corridor
note: advisory and technical support from a private foundation and an open-source payments foundation; no transaction volume, participant count or fee schedule is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cost of sending money within Africa
position_end: Put at 8.78% of the amount sent against the SDG target of 3% (2026-08)
note: the figure is cited by AfricaNenda's deputy chief executive in an interview rather than drawn from a published series, and no date, corridor set or methodology is given for it, so it is a stated position and not a measurement the base can reproduce

subject: dpi.pay
name: Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS)
milestone: BEAC acceded on 2026-07-11
position_start: Operating from January 2022 across West and East African cores, with no Central African central bank participating
position_end: Extended into Central Africa by the BEAC's accession, wired into a national switch in Kenya for the first time, and carrying a wallet-based Nigeria-to-Ghana rail settled in naira

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSSCARD
milestone: Launched with Afreximbank and Mercury Payment Services
position_end: A continental card scheme launched to route African card payments inside the continent rather than through global networks; no issuance, volume or country coverage held
sources: 2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment Systems Directive for Africa (PSDA)
milestone: Decision 21 of the AACB Assembly of Governors, 2025-11-28
position_end: Directed to be led by central banks rather than an external entity, with the Assembly's own task force on payment system integration to lead harmonisation; no draft directive held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Stablecoin settlement rails serving African cross-border payments
milestone: Argued as moving from speculation to settlement infrastructure, 2026-08-17
position_end: Described by a pan-African payments operator's product chief as moving from speculative use into the plumbing of remittances and business settlement, on the evidence of Mastercard's agreement to acquire BVNK at up to US$1.8bn and Visa's stablecoin-card expansion through Stripe's Bridge into more than 100 countries, African markets among them; a first named African deployment is Flutterwave's tie-up with Caliza offering USD accounts with USDC and USDT conversion
note: an operator's account of its own market rather than a regulatory or central-bank position; no African regulator's treatment of stablecoin settlement is held. Flutterwave and Caliza announced on 2026-08-13 dedicated USD accounts for African businesses on ACH, Fedwire, RTP and SWIFT with stablecoin conversion, aimed at cross-border transfers above US$1m and at cutting dependence on correspondent banking - a commercial announcement carrying no volume, pricing or licensing detail

subject: dpi.pay
name: Unmet trade finance demand
position_end: US$74bn to US$100bn of unmet trade finance demand, with commercial banks intermediating about 23% of the continent's trade against 40% over 2011 to 2019, and intra-African trade at US$213.8bn in 2025 (2026-08)
note: a research firm's policy brief, which names digital payment rails, blockchain-enabled trade infrastructure and factoring as the routes to closing the gap

subject: dpi.mis
name: Africa CDC Central Data Repository
milestone: Launched 2026-01-28
position_end: A federated repository integrating national surveillance, laboratory and programme data in which member states retain ownership of their data
sources: 2026-01-28 Africa CDC Establishes Central Data Repository to Strengthen Public Health Surveillance
note: Financed by the Global Fund and prototyped by the Public Health Informatics Institute

subject: dpi.mis
name: African Regional Integration Synthesized Index (ASRII) platform
milestone: ECOWAS Commission trained on the platform, Abuja, 4-7 August 2026
position_end: The African Union Commission's platform for submission, validation, automated computation and dissemination of regional integration scores across political, economic, infrastructure, and human and social pillars, developed with the regional economic communities, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Development Bank to replace manual data collection. Deployment to the regional economic communities began with a four-day training of 20 core participants at the ECOWAS Commission in Abuja on 4-7 August 2026, at which its Secretary General said the Commission holds no centralised database of the status, amendments and implications of regional legal protocols
note: The platform is to be used by the regional economic communities to evaluate member states' policy implementation; no published score, methodology note or coverage list is held

subject: gov.policy
name: Africa Technology Policy Tracker
milestone: No launch date published
position_end: A continental register built by the Carnegie Endowment with the African Telecommunications Union, consolidating national digital-economy laws, policies and regulations across infrastructure, platforms, skills and innovation; it indexes adopted documents only, weights nothing and assesses neither implementation nor rights compatibility. The counts reported on 2026-07-30 are 60 documents for Nigeria, 59 for Rwanda and 19 for Zambia
note: Neither the launch date nor the number of countries covered is established

subject: gov.policy
name: Anti-IFFs Policy Tracker
milestone: Continental roll-out endorsed by Ministerial Declaration, joint 9th STC on Finance and 5th STC on Trade, Abidjan, 20-24 July 2026
position_start: Piloted eighteen months in Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, Namibia, Uganda and Zambia, built by Tax Justice Network Africa with the AU Commission's ETTIM department and the African Tax Administration Forum
position_end: Endorsed for continental roll-out as a standing self-assessment instrument scoring anti-IFF policy, legal, institutional and data-sharing frameworks; no roll-out timetable, country list or governance body named

subject: gov.policy
name: AUDA-NEPAD island economies programme
milestone: Launched at Abidjan, 2026-07-24
position_end: A country-owned framework for seven island states built around industrialisation, digitalisation, corridors and AI, in partnership with the Republic of Korea; the ministerial communique adopting it is not published

subject: gov.regional
name: AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade
milestone: Eight calls to action adopted at the close of the second Digital Trade Forum, Lagos, 2026-07-02
position_start: Adopted by the AU Assembly in 2024, with a Digital Identity Annex adopted in February 2025 and no implementation forum held
position_end: State parties committed to expedite ratification and domestication under eight calls to action; no ratification count is published with them; the calls carry no enforcement mechanism, no ratification deadline and no named financing

subject: gov.regional
name: AfCFTA Secretariat
milestone: 18th Council of Ministers, Abuja, 2026-07-09
position_start: Council bureau chaired by Egypt; the digital trade protocol adopted but no forum convened on it
position_end: Nigeria in the chair with digital trade among four stated priorities, a second digital trade forum held and a data-exchange system of the Secretariat's own launched
sources: 2026-07-09 Nigeria Takes AfCFTA Council Chair as Digital Forum Charts Roadmap for Implementation|2026-07-07 African nations recommit to operationalize AfCFTA digital single market framework

subject: gov.regional
name: African Financial Stability Committee
milestone: Continental portal launched by the Central Bank of Egypt, 2026-08-03
position_end: Hosted by the Association of African Central Banks and running a Macroprudential Policy Development and Implementation Working Group and an African Financial Stability Report Working Group; the continental portal carrying its mandate, structure, member central banks, meeting calendar and working groups was built and launched by the Central Bank of Egypt rather than by the association's secretariat, executing a decision of the 47th Assembly of Governors of 2025-11-28
note: The portal's URL and a launch date distinct from the Central Bank of Egypt's statement of 2026-08-03 are not held

subject: gov.regional
name: African Financial Stability Report
milestone: Inaugural 2024-2025 edition released, July 2026
position_end: Inaugural 2024-2025 edition endorsed for publication by the Association of African Central Banks' 47th Assembly of Governors at Yaounde on 2025-11-28 and released in July 2026, covering 46 countries on data as at December 2024 with analysis through 2025. Its payments chapter, built from 26 central banks' published data, records that about 67 per cent of the continent's payment infrastructures are national systems run by central banks and 56 per cent of established systems handle retail, and finds the landscape fragmented, interoperability still limited and the operationalisation of regional and pan-African systems facing continuing challenges
note: Whether the report has been published on the committee's portal is not established

subject: gov.regional
name: African Telecommunications Union (ATU)
milestone: Headquarters return to Kinshasa ratified 2026-07-23 at the 7th Plenipotentiary Conference
position_start: Under the mandate set at the sixth session in Algiers in 2022, chaired by Algeria
position_end: A secretary general elected for the next four-year term, a 25-state administrative council seated, the chairmanship passed to Nigeria and a ministerial declaration adopted; the union's plenipotentiary conference ratified the return of its headquarters to Kinshasa on 23 July 2026, after the host state paid more than US$1.4m in arrears, with no date stated for the move
note: Kezias Kazuba Mwale of Zambia takes office on 2027-01-01 for four years

subject: gov.regional
name: African Union Commission
milestone: Cooperation agreement signed with the ITU, Geneva, 2026-07
position_start: Author of the Continental AI Strategy and the Digital Transformation Strategy, with no continental digital partnership agreement on record in the year before
position_end: Two cooperation instruments signed inside six months, with a US technology company and with the ITU, and a coordinated African position taken to the first global AI-governance dialogue
sources: 2026-07-16 African Union Commission, ITU sign cooperation agreement|2026-02-20 AUC Signs Partnership With Google|2026-07-09 African Union pushes for unified African voice at Global AI Governance Dialogue

subject: gov.regional
name: AFRINIC governance and receivership
status: Implemented, board contested and the receiver undischarged
milestone: Governance committee constituted 2026-08-17
position_end: The regional internet registry named a person to all eight board seats on 12 September 2025 while withholding every candidate vote tally its own election guidelines promised; the purported board and the undischarged receiver announced close collaboration from 13 October 2025 without publishing which office could sign, pay or veto, and no court order, delegation, bank mandate or responsibility matrix has been located behind it; the receiver appointed an audit firm on 13 October 2025 to audit three overdue financial years without an annual meeting, with no published appointment date, executed instrument, statutory route, remuneration decision or independence review; ordinary resolutions on US$3.29m of disputed legal spending, put to the June 2026 annual meeting, were still unresolved on the public record 46 days later; six regional members were named to a bylaws review committee without disclosing which constituents each represents; a member's challenge to the board's ratification of a policy draft remains open with an interim application declined and no reasoned merits decision; the appeal court set aside the registry's 2023 appeal for want of corporate authority without ruling on the receiver's permission or on statutory leave; and a governance committee of three elected and two board-appointed voting members was constituted on 17 August 2026 on terms running to the ends of 2027, 2028 and 2029
note: most of the account is one outlet's documentary analysis of the registry's own filings and public docket, alongside the registry's own announcements; a proposal for continental internet-governance coordination raises the unresolved question of what authority any new council would hold over the registry's decisions

subject: gov.regional
name: Algiers Declaration on African Telecommunications Sovereignty and Integrated Connectivity 2026-2030
milestone: Adopted by ministers at Algiers, 2026-03
position_end: Adopted as a continental position on integrated terrestrial, submarine and satellite infrastructure, local data centres, exchange points and cybersecurity; no work programme or text held

subject: gov.regional
name: ATU Strategic Plan 2027-2031
milestone: Comments on the draft due to the Secretary-General by 2026-06-23
position_end: A draft Strategic Plan for 2027-2031 was circulated to member states for comment ahead of CPL-26; the draft is not published, and no adopted plan, budget or final acts of the conference are held
note: The conference elected a secretary general and seated an administrative council in July 2026; no adopted plan or budget was published with them

subject: gov.regional
name: Digital Parliaments Project Africa
milestone: Launched at a capacity-training event, Parliament of Ghana, 2026-08-06
position_end: Launch cohort of the parliaments of Ghana, Botswana and South Africa, the National Assemblies of the Gambia and Senegal, and the Pan-African Parliament, led by the POPVOX-DPP Foundation with the House Democracy Partnership; no amount, duration, funder or work programme stated

subject: gov.regional
name: Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation ministerial framework
milestone: Eighth ministerial conference convened for Seoul, 8-11 September 2026
position_end: Eighth ministerial set for Seoul under the theme of artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure, convened by the continental development bank with new co-financing expected
note: a media advisory issued in advance; what the conference produces is not yet on record, and nothing here states a figure

subject: gov.regional

subject: gov.regional
name: Smart Africa Alliance
milestone: Two expressions of interest issued 2026-08-13, closing 31 August
position_start: 37 member states, working to the previous strategy
position_end: 42 member states and a three-year strategy whose flagships are a data exchange, an innovation platform and digital identity; the secretariat issued two calls for expressions of interest on 13 August, one for content-delivery providers across broadband, data governance and cybersecurity and green-digital domains, and one for a consultancy to draft a gender-inclusion strategy for women's participation in ICT policymaking and governance, both closing on 31 August

subject: gov.standards
name: African Common Proposals for WRC-27
milestone: Third African preparatory meeting convened for Tunis, 7-11 September 2026, contributions closing 2026-08-23
position_end: Preliminary African Common Proposals for WRC-27 and RA-27 are to be consolidated from the recommendations of the African Telecommunications Union's WRC-27 working groups at the third African Preparatory Meeting, Tunis, 7-11 September 2026, co-organised with Tunisia's Agence Nationale des Frequences; no proposal text is published
note: Convened by ATU circular Ref. 073/07/ATU/ARD/CIR-2026, issued from Nairobi on 2026-07-07

subject: gov.standards
name: AFRINIC Constitution (Bylaws)
milestone: Second consultation draft open for comment 4 to 21 August 2026
position_end: Fifth version in force since December 2020; the Bylaws Review Committee ran a first consultation from 2026-04-20, extended on 2026-05-08 to close 2026-05-17, and published a draft amended Constitution on 2026-08-04 for a second consultation closing 2026-08-21. It names membership, powers of members, the Nomination Committee and appointment of directors as the most heavily revised provisions, and a new Article 3 would write into the constitution that AFRINIC is the Regional Internet Registry for Africa and the Indian Ocean and that its governance will be periodically reviewed against internationally recognised governance standards. The published-draft milestone slipped about six weeks against the Committee's own indicative timetable while the Special General Members Meeting stayed in September 2026, and no consolidation or analysis of the first round's submissions is published; a second draft was open for comment from 4 to 21 August 2026. Proposed article 9.8 would let a two-thirds board vote revoke the nomination committee and restart an election the board itself had judged to have failed, with the same board defining the failure, deciding the case and triggering the consequence before any independent review; the current rule barring a conflicted director from voting would be dropped and recusal relocated into board policy, which matters because Mauritius company law lets an interested director vote after disclosure unless the constitution says otherwise; article 16 opens a wide advice channel with no register of advice given or received; and article 17.5 would create an acting chief executive office with no maximum term and no stated link to board seat 9 or to removal rules. A cyberdiplomacy consultant who had opposed early constitutional reform argued on 19 August that the article-by-article rationale now gives members enough to test the draft against the failures it is meant to fix
note: The rationales for Article 24, governing law and dispute resolution, and for the Board's power to terminate membership are recorded as awaiting external legal opinion

subject: gov.standards
name: Continental ICT standardisation alignment
milestone: Alignment talks opened between the telecoms union, the standards organisation and a standardisation partnership
position_end: Talks opened on a coordinated continental approach across the standards lifecycle, from development through harmonised adoption and implementation by countries, naming fragmentation and the failure to translate continental and international standards into national frameworks as the problem
note: no instrument, work programme or timetable follows from the talks on the record

subject: gov.protect
name: African Union Data Policy Framework
milestone: Alignment measured at about a third of member states, reported 2026-08-11
position_end: In force as the continental reference framework, with about a third of the 54 member states aligned to it on a 2026-08-11 analysis, and 25 national regulatory sandboxes recorded across 15 countries by late 2024; no compliance mechanism, reporting cycle or enforcement route is stated
note: the alignment figure is an analyst estimate rather than an African Union count

subject: gov.protect
name: Malabo Convention
milestone: In force since 2023-06-08, on the fifteenth ratification
position_start: In force, and the continental benchmark against which national data-protection regimes are measured
position_end: Unchanged in text; a majority of the Union's 55 members remain outside it twelve years after adoption

subject: gov.protect
name: Signatures and ratifications of the Malabo Convention
position_start: 21 of 55 signed, 20 ratified or acceded and 20 deposited (2026-02-02, the depositary's register)
position_end: Equatorial Guinea, where the Convention was adopted and after whose then-capital it is named, signed on 2026-07-28 and has not deposited an instrument of ratification
note: The register is dated 2026-02-02; no later register is held

subject: include.divides
name: Women and girls digital-inclusion accelerator
milestone: Next call for solutions opened, applications due 2026-08-17
position_end: An industry-body accelerator backed by two private foundations opened its next call for digital-inclusion solutions for women and girls across India and sub-Saharan Africa, with a grant amount listed at INR 42,000,000
note: the grant figure is the announcement's own and covers both regions; no African allocation, cohort size or award is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Africa AI Council
milestone: Established by the Smart Africa Board at Conakry, 2025-11-17
position_end: Established under a board of 42 heads of state with the AU Commissioner for Energy and Infrastructure and the ITU Secretary-General; no work programme or output held in the nine months since

subject: tech.ai
name: Africa AI Fund
milestone: Announced at Kigali, April 2025
position_start: Announced in April 2025 at US$60bn, alongside the Africa AI Declaration, with nothing capitalised
position_end: Still cited as one pillar of the continental AI architecture; no capitalisation, governance structure or disbursement held
sources: 2026-05-21 Pushing back from Big Tech Africa's hard road to AI sovereignty

subject: tech.ai
name: AU Continental AI Strategy
milestone: Adopted by the AU Executive Council, 45th Ordinary Session, Accra, 2024-07-19
position_start: Adopted 2024-07-19 as the continental reference for national AI policy, on an implementation timeframe running 2025 to 2030
position_end: Unchanged in text, and the reference the Commission carried into global forums; ministers meeting at the ECA called for its translation into national frameworks. The instrument's own timetable runs Phase I across 2025-2026, a midterm review in 2027 and Phase II from 2028
sources: 2024-07-19-au-continental-artificial-intelligence-strategy|2026-04-13 Stakeholders urge shift in digital public infrastructure trajectory|2026-07-09 African Union pushes for unified African voice at Global AI Governance Dialogue
note: Its annex records six member states with standalone national AI strategies at drafting in July 2024

subject: tech.ai
name: Common African Position on AI and its Impact on Peace, Security, Democracy and Development
milestone: Peace and Security Council requested finalisation, 1339th meeting, 2026-04-16
position_end: The Council requested the Commission to expedite the comprehensive study and the Common African Position and submit them for its consideration; a Policy Brief on AI for Peace, Security and Governance in Africa is reported in progress and no text is published
note: Drafted by the Commission with the AI Advisory Group on Governance, Peace and Security

subject: tech.ai
name: Monitoring and evaluation of the AU Continental AI Strategy
milestone: Peace and Security Council requested periodic reports, 1339th meeting, 2026-04-16
position_start: Provided for in the Strategy through an African AI readiness index, a public monitoring dashboard and regional AI observatories, with nothing published
position_end: Still nothing published; the Peace and Security Council requested the Commission and its AI Advisory Group to submit periodic reports on 2026-04-16, and the Strategy's own midterm review falls in 2027

subject: tech.innovate
name: Multi-country mapping of innovation-support organisations
milestone: Procurement opened, bids due 2026-08-17
position_end: A EUR120,000 procurement opened by a European development agency for a multi-country mapping of African entrepreneurship- and innovation-support organisations under a Europe-Africa digital innovation programme
note: a procurement rather than an award; no supplier, country list or publication commitment for the mapping is stated

subject: geopol.usa
name: America First Global Health Strategy data-sharing agreements
milestone: Health cooperation memorandums signed with more than 30 countries since December 2025
movement: Advanced, refused by three states on data terms
position_start: Did not exist; no bilateral United States health agreement of this kind on record before December 2025
position_end: Memorandums worth US$20bn signed with more than 30 countries since December 2025, on a model Data Sharing Agreement giving the United States at-will access to seven classes of national health system for 25 years with a 10-year post-termination tail; Ghana refused in April 2026, Zimbabwe withdrew in February 2026 and Zambia shelved in May 2026, and Kenya's framework is before the Court of Appeal with a final ruling due at the end of October 2026; the State Department's standard-form memorandum, held as a blank template dated 2026-03-11, commits a partner government to name and run its electronic medical record, laboratory, pharmacy, surveillance, commodity-inventory and national data warehouse systems, to load 90 per cent of clinical encounters into the electronic medical record within two years of rollout in a facility, to enter a data sharing agreement expected to run twenty-five years, and to provide specimens and genetic sequence data of pathogens with epidemic potential within five days of detection, with section 4.7 making failure on those commitments grounds for changing or discontinuing the assistance; the signed texts are withheld, the department having published a subset of the memorandums in March 2026 and then removed public access, and a freedom-of-information suit covering sixteen African countries (Public Citizen v. Department of State, No. 1:26-cv-01137, D.D.C.) was unresolved when filed on 2026-04-02
note: The model Data Sharing Agreement's own text is not held; its terms are reported at second hand (2025-11-15). The standard-form memorandum is held as a blank template and is not any signatory's instrument

subject: geopol.usa
name: US-AUC Strategic Investment Working Group
milestone: Launch announced in a joint statement, 2026-01-28
position_end: Agreed to channel US private investment into AU-backed infrastructure including digital transformation, on an investment-in-place-of-aid posture; no membership, meeting or work programme held
sources: 2026-01-28 Joint Statement of the United States and African Union on the Launch of a Strategic Investment Working Group

subject: geopol.china
name: China-Africa Digital Cooperation Development Action Plan
milestone: Issued at the China-Africa Digital Cooperation Forum, Beijing, 2024-07-29
position_start: Issued 2024-07-29 by China and 26 African states across six cooperation actions, with a three-year target of ten joint digital transformation demonstration projects and 1,000 personnel trained
position_end: Unchanged; no progress report, no accession beyond the original 26 states and no delivery against the three-year targets is held
note: Signed by states individually rather than by the African Union; no sum appears anywhere in the plan

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese artificial-intelligence cooperation centres with the African Union
milestone: Announced 2026-08-16
position_end: China says it will establish artificial-intelligence application cooperation centres with the African Union and offer developing countries 5,000 training places over five years; no site, budget, term or agreement text is stated
note: the account is Chinese state media's, framed against a reported American push to make allies choose sides on artificial intelligence, and adds continental detail absent from the wire report it cites

subject: geopol.eu
name: AU-Germany strategic dialogue
milestone: Held at Addis Ababa, 2026-07-15
position_start: No dated session held in the base
position_end: Reviewed the partnership and named AI governance and cybersecurity among the areas for cooperation, within a dialogue that is principally about peace and security

subject: finance.new
name: Africa Finance Corporation digital bond
position_end: CHF 350m raised on a five-year digital bond listed, traded and settled on a regulated digital exchange — stated as the first by an African institution — priced at a 1.4925% coupon and arranged by two European banks; it is the issuer’s fourth and largest Swiss franc issuance

subject: finance.new
name: Africa50 Infrastructure Acceleration Fund
milestone: Fourth close reaches about US$330m on British International Investment's US$20m commitment, Infra for Africa Forum 2026, 2026-08-10
position_end: Fourth close of about US$330m, joined by British International Investment's US$20m commitment alongside the African Development Bank, the International Finance Corporation and more than 20 African institutional investors; the fund, managed by Africa Infrastructure Investment Partners, directs capital to logistics, power, water and sanitation and social infrastructure as well as digital connectivity; the size and date of earlier closes are not established
note: Digital connectivity is one of several sectors the fund targets, not a digital-only vehicle; British International Investment's commitment is undifferentiated fund capital rather than a sector-tagged sub-commitment

subject: finance.new
name: BIASHARA 2063 project (AU Commission institutional systems)
milestone: Wireless infrastructure tender issued, 2026-07-27
position_end: A World Bank-financed programme building the Commission's own institutions and systems, procuring wireless infrastructure for its headquarters; no envelope, timetable or results framework held
note: The tender names the credit but not the operation's size

subject: finance.new
name: Capital raised by startups from a technology company's African accelerators
milestone: Stated by the company 2026-08-07
position_end: More than US$1bn raised cumulatively since 2017, with a stated survival rate above 90% against a 70-80% failure rate for the wider ecosystem (2026-08)
note: the company's own figure, with no cohort list, methodology or definition of survival published, and the comparison rate is not sourced in the account

subject: finance.new
name: Development-finance and infrastructure-fund partnership
milestone: Partnership strengthened, reported 2026-08-13
position_end: A British development finance institution and a continental infrastructure fund announced a strengthened partnership to scale infrastructure financing across Africa, connectivity among the named sectors; no commitment amount, fund vehicle, country allocation or timetable is published
note: no finance record was built: the accounts state no commitment amount

subject: finance.new
name: EU Multiannual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027
milestone: Amended at the NDICI-Global Europe mid-term review by Commission Implementing Decision C(2024)7502
position_start: EUR 490m for priority area 4, Digital and Science, Technology and Innovation, of which EUR 240m for digital transformation, within a regional envelope of EUR 12,000m
position_end: Unchanged; the mid-term review cut priority area 4 from EUR 1,240m to EUR 490m and its digital transformation component from EUR 940m to EUR 240m, or 2.0 per cent of an envelope enlarged from EUR 10,242m to EUR 12,000m, and no later amendment is held
note: The decision carries no date in its text and is placed in 2024 by its decision number alone

subject: finance.new
name: Foundation call for AI in family planning
milestone: Call opened, closing 2026-08-25
position_end: A private foundation opened a call for proposals using artificial intelligence to widen access to digital contraception information across sub-Saharan Africa, offering up to US$500,000 a project, with applications closing on 25 August 2026
note: a call rather than an award: no envelope total, number of grants, eligibility detail or decision date is published

subject: finance.new
name: Growth-capital investment in a pan-African messaging infrastructure provider
milestone: US$12m investment reported 2026-08-11
position_end: US$12m into a provider of application-to-person messaging — one-time passwords, transaction alerts and delivery updates — operating across 35 African countries through 15 operator partnerships
note: the instrument type is not further specified in the record; the rails carried here are what one-time passwords and transaction alerts run on, which places a private messaging vendor inside the payment estate

subject: finance.new
name: Hewlett Foundation grant to BudgIT (general operating support)
milestone: Committed 2026-03-10, US$500,000 of US$1,000,000 disbursed
position_end: US$1,000,000 committed (US$500,000 disbursed) as general operating support to BudgIT's budget-transparency and civic-tech work

subject: finance.new
name: Hewlett Foundation grant to BudgIT (learning systems and communications)
milestone: Committed 2026-02-24, fully disbursed
position_end: US$50,000 committed and fully disbursed to strengthen BudgIT's learning systems and strategic communications

subject: finance.new
name: Hewlett Foundation grant to Cenfri (digital transformation programme)
milestone: Committed 2026-03-21, US$150,000 of US$300,000 disbursed
position_end: US$300,000 committed (US$150,000 disbursed) to renew Cenfri's work on digital transformation and its link to evidence-informed policymaking across Africa

subject: finance.new
name: Hewlett Foundation grant to Data4Change (Data Hub: Africa)
milestone: Committed 2026-02-12, US$200,000 of US$400,000 disbursed
position_end: US$400,000 committed (US$200,000 disbursed) to Data4Change's Africa Hub, building community-generated evidence for policy and practice in East and West Africa

subject: finance.new
name: Hewlett Foundation grant to ICED (AI-enabled evidence generation)
milestone: Committed 2026-03-16, fully disbursed
position_end: US$100,000 committed and fully disbursed for the International Centre for Evaluation and Development to adopt AI-enabled evidence generation institution-wide

subject: finance.new
name: IFC equity investment in Jumia
milestone: US$25m equity announced 2026-08-12
position_end: US$25m of IFC equity inside a wider US$50m raise
note: the World Bank Group's private-sector arm taking equity in a listed pan-African e-commerce platform operating in eight countries; the stated development case is about 60,000 annual active sellers reaching wider markets, around 1,800 direct jobs and income for more than 100,000 independent sales agents, all of them the investor's own projections rather than measured outcomes, and none carries a date by which it is to be tested

subject: finance.new
name: LINGUA Africa language-model grants
milestone: 26 projects selected from an open call that closed 15 June 2026
position_end: 26 projects covering more than 50 African languages, dialects and sign languages across 47 countries, each awardee eligible for up to US$250,000 in cash and US$400,000 in compute credits; health, agriculture and justice are the stated use cases
note: funded jointly by a philanthropic foundation, two American technology companies and an African research collective; no single total is published and the individual shares are not disclosed, so the programme's size can only be bounded from the per-award ceiling

subject: finance.new
name: TaxDev III (IFS tax and social-protection policy data programme)
milestone: Running 2023-2030, US$6.36m disbursed across 29 transactions (as at 2026-08)
position_end: Institute for Fiscal Studies programme, funded by the UK's FCDO, building tax and social-protection policy data resources and tools with finance ministries and revenue authorities in Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and Uganda; about US$6.36m disbursed 2023-2026

subject: finance.mou

milestone: Signed at Addis Ababa, 2026-02-17
position_end: Signed on AI and cloud infrastructure, skills, research and AI policy, with a pledge to train three million students and teachers by 2030

milestone: Signed at the AI for Good summit, Geneva, 2026-07
position_end: Signed across AI, digital public infrastructure, skills, connectivity, cybersecurity, space technology and standards, naming the Commission the continental coordinating partner for the 55 member states
sources: 2026-07-16 African Union Commission, ITU sign cooperation agreement
